title: Rab Prices & Budget 2027: What a Trip Really Costs
metaDescription: Rab, Croatia 2027 budget: ferry fares, apartment rates, restaurant prices and daily costs for budget, mid-range and luxury trips, with money-saving tips.
content:
## How Much Does a Trip to Rab Cost in 2027?

Rab is a moderately priced Adriatic island. It costs less than Dubrovnik, Hvar or Split, but more than inland Croatia. Prices are driven by season more than anything else. A week in July or August can cost 40–60% more than the same week in late May or September.

The 2027 figures below are projections built on 2026 prices, which are the latest confirmed data. Expect increases of about 3–8% on accommodation and dining, and smaller changes on ferry fares, which are set by the ferry operator and revised less often.

### Daily Budget per Person (2027 Estimate)

- **Budget: €70–110.** Private apartment or campsite shared between two, self-catering with one konoba meal, free beaches.
- **Mid-range: €130–190.** Private apartment or 3–4★ hotel, restaurant lunch or dinner daily, a boat trip, rental scooter or bikes.
- **Luxury: €280+.** Heritage hotel or villa, seafood dinners, private boat charter.

These figures exclude transport to Croatia. They assume two people sharing a room, which lowers the per-person accommodation cost.

## How Have Prices in Rab Changed Recently?

Since Croatia adopted the euro in January 2023, prices on the islands have moved upward in three areas: accommodation, restaurants and parking.

- **Accommodation:** Budget apartments and guesthouses now typically start at €40–90 per night, mid-range apartments and 3–4★ hotels at €90–180, and high-end hotels or villas at €180–500+ in peak season.
- **Restaurants:** A main course in a mid-range restaurant is commonly quoted at €20–35 in 2026, while simple konobas stay closer to €15–25. Fine dining runs €40–70 per main.
- **Ferries:** Fares on the main route stayed comparatively stable. The 2026 high-season foot-passenger fare is €4.20 and the low-season fare is €2.50.
- **Cakes and snacks:** A slice of Rab cake (rapska torta) costs about €5–7.

The practical result: restaurants and waterfront locations in Rab Town have become the least forgiving part of the budget, while self-catering and out-of-town accommodation still offer good value.

## Accommodation Prices in Rab

### Rab Town

Old Town apartments average €60–90 per night in May or October and €120–180 in July and August. Among hotels, Hotel Arbiana sits 50 m from the harbor and is priced around €110–180 per night in shoulder season, rising considerably in summer. Grand Hotel Imperial is at the upper end, from about €180 per night in shoulder season to €350+ in July and August.

### Banjol, Palit and Barbat

These villages around Rab Town offer the lowest rates on the island. Apartments in Banjol, known for sandy shallow beaches, can be found for €40–60 per night in shoulder season and €60–120 in summer. Banjol is within about 3 km of Rab Town.

### Lopar

Lopar is the base for sandy beaches, including Paradise Beach (Rajska plaža), about 12 km from Rab Town. Apartments range from €50–80 per night in shoulder season and €70–150 in peak season. Resorts cost €150–300+. Several campsites are also located here.

### Kampor

Kampor, northwest of Rab Town, has apartments and villas among pine trees. Apartments cost about €80–180 per night in summer and hotels €150–300+.

**Opinion:** A hotel in Rab Town in August is poor value. A private apartment in Banjol or Lopar costs half as much, and the Old Town is a short bus ride or scooter trip away. Spend the difference on a boat trip.

## Getting to Rab: Ferry Prices and Timetable

### Stinica–Mišnjak (Main Route)

The Stinica–Mišnjak crossing takes about 20 minutes and is the cheapest and most frequent route to Rab. It is operated by Rapska plovidba. Current published fares:

- **Foot passenger:** €2.50 in low season, €4.20 in high season (1 May–29 September in 2026).
- **Child 3–12:** €1.10 low season, €1.60 high season.
- **Car up to 5 m long and 2 m high:** €12.70 low season, €18.20 high season.
- **Longer or taller vehicle:** €20.00 low season, €22.80 high season.

Departures run through the day from about 04:00 to after 22:00, with a late-night sailing around midnight in summer. Check the current timetable before travel, since sailing times shift by season.

A car with two passengers on the high-season fare costs about €26.60 each way, so a return trip adds roughly €53 to the budget. Out of season it is about €17.70 each way.

### Other Routes

Jadrolinija runs seasonal links to Rab from Senj (from about €15 for foot passengers, 2h 15m), Kraljevica (from about €10) and Valbiska on Krk to Lopar (about €4.50 for foot passengers). These run mostly June to August, only on some days, and suit visitors coming from Krk or the north coast. For most visitors arriving by car from Zagreb, Rijeka or Zadar, Stinica is the practical choice.

**Insider tip:** In July and August, queues at Stinica build quickly on Saturdays. Crossing before 08:00 or after 18:00 shortens the wait considerably.

## Food and Restaurant Prices in Rab

| Item | Typical price |
|---|---|
| Konoba main course | €15–25 |
| Mid-range restaurant main | €20–35 |
| Seafood main with a view (e.g., Lopar waterfront) | €20–40 |
| Fine dining main | €40–70 |
| Three courses with drinks | €30–50 per person |
| Dinner for two, mid-range konoba | €40–70 |
| Rab cake, one slice | €5–7 |

Restaurant San Marino in Lopar is known for fresh seafood, with mains from €20–40. In Rab Town, konobas close to the main street serve peka and grilled fish at €15–25 per main course.

### How to Cut Food Costs

- Eat the main meal at lunch. Many konobas serve a cheaper midday menu (marenda) than the dinner menu.
- Buy groceries at the supermarkets in Rab Town, Banjol and Lopar. A self-catered breakfast and a picnic lunch lower the daily food cost to about €20–30 per person.
- Order fish by the kilogram only after asking the price. Whole fish is usually priced per kg and can raise a bill by €20–40.
- Skip the waterfront tables on the harbor for dinner on busy nights. A street one block back charges less for the same dishes.

## Activities, Beaches and Local Transport

- **Beaches:** Most are free. Paradise Beach is free to enter, with parking at €5–10 per day.
- **Bell tower climb, Rab Town:** about €3–5.
- **Boat excursions:** €30–60 per person for a full day, around €45 for a half-day trip.
- **Scooter rental:** €30–45 for 24 hours.
- **Local bus:** €1.80–2.50 for a single ticket within about 10 km.

The island is small, about 22 km long, so a car is optional if staying in or near Rab Town. Visitors who plan to stay in Lopar and Rab Town can use buses and a scooter for a few days instead of paying for a ferry car crossing.

## Sample 2027 Budgets for a 7-Night Stay (Two People)

### Budget (shoulder season, car)

- Apartment, 7 nights at €55–70: €385–490
- Ferry return, car and two adults, low season: about €35 + €10 = roughly €45
- Food, mostly self-catered with two konoba dinners: €280–350
- Parking, snacks, bus: €60–90
- **Total: about €770–975**, or €55–70 per person per day.

### Mid-range (June or September)

- Apartment or 3–4★ hotel, 7 nights at €100–150: €700–1,050
- Ferry return, mid-season: €50–55
- Food, restaurant meal daily: €560–800
- One boat trip, scooter two days, entry fees: €170–250
- **Total: about €1,500–2,150**, or roughly €105–155 per person per day.

### Peak summer (July–August)

- Apartment, 7 nights at €120–180: €840–1,260
- Ferry return, high season: about €53
- Food: €700–950
- Activities and parking: €200–350
- **Total: about €1,800–2,600** for two, before adding a 5–8% projected 2027 increase.

## Best Time to Visit Rab for Lower Prices

Shoulder season (May–June and September–October) cuts accommodation prices by 20–40%. The ferry fare also drops once the high-season period ends in late September. The sea is warm enough for swimming from roughly late May to early October, so September gives the best balance of price and water temperature. Many smaller konobas and some shops close from November to March, which limits options in winter.

## 2027 Money-Saving Tips for Rab

- Book apartments before March for summer 2027. Owners of private units often hold the lowest rates for early bookings.
- Choose Banjol, Palit or Lopar over Rab Town for the cheapest beds.
- Travel on foot to the ferry only if staying near Mišnjak or Rab Town. Taking a car costs about five times more than a foot passenger fare.
- Carry cash for small konobas and parking machines, though cards are widely accepted in town.
- Check whether parking in Rab Town is included in the apartment price. Paid zones near the Old Town fill early in summer.

## Frequently Asked Questions

See the FAQ section below for the most common budget questions.

faq.question: Is Rab expensive compared with other Croatian islands?
faq.answer: Rab is mid-priced. Peak-season apartments cost €80–180 per night and mains €15–25 in konobas, well below Hvar or Dubrovnik. It is more expensive than mainland inland towns.

faq.question: How much does the ferry to Rab cost in 2027?
faq.answer: The 2026 Stinica–Mišnjak fares are €2.50 (low season) and €4.20 (high season) for adults, and €12.70 or €18.20 for a car up to 5 m. 2027 fares are not confirmed, but small increases are likely.

faq.question: What is a realistic daily budget for Rab in 2027?
faq.answer: Plan on €70–110 per person for budget travel, €130–190 for mid-range and €280+ for luxury. These figures assume two people share a room and exclude travel to Croatia.

faq.question: What is the cheapest month to visit Rab?
faq.answer: May, early June, late September and October are the cheapest options for good weather. Accommodation drops 20–40% from the July–August level, and ferry fares fall to the low-season rate once the high-season period ends.

faq.question: How much is a meal in Rab?
faq.answer: A konoba main costs €15–25, while a three-course meal with drinks averages €30–50 per person. Dinner for two at a mid-range konoba is usually €40–70.

faq.question: Do you need a car on Rab?
faq.answer: Not if staying in Rab Town, Banjol or Lopar. Buses cost €1.80–2.50 per ride and a scooter costs €30–45 per day. A car adds €12.70–18.20 per ferry crossing plus parking.

faq.question: Are the beaches on Rab free?
faq.answer: Most are free. Paradise Beach in Lopar has no entry fee, though parking costs €5–10 per day. Sun loungers and umbrellas at organised beaches are charged separately.

quickAnswer: A realistic 2027 budget for Rab is about €70–110 per person per day for budget travel, €130–190 for mid-range and €280+ for luxury. Peak-season apartments run €80–180 per night, konoba mains €15–25, and the Stinica–Mišnjak ferry costs €12–18 for a car. Expect rises of roughly 3–8% over 2026.
